coordinates.locator: Nominatim result for "Kolar Gold Fields" (node 245614133): Kolar Gold Fields, Kolar Gold Field taluk, Kolar, Karnataka, 563115, India
coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the OpenStreetMap place node of the town of Kolar Gold Fields. The gold mines (Champion Reef and others) extend over several kilometres around it and no fetched source gives the shaft or hall of the experiments.

depth_mwe.note: The paper quotes the depth of the Phase I detector as 7000 hg/cm^2; 1 hg/cm^2 = 100 g/cm^2 = 1 metre of water equivalent, so the figure is 7000 m.w.e. The Phase II detector was at 6045 hg/cm^2. This is the deepest of the experiment levels, not an average for the site.
depth_mwe.quote: was installed deep underground at the depth of 7000 hg/cm2

summary.plain: The deep Kolar Gold Fields gold mines in southern India, where Indian-Japanese teams ran underground cosmic-ray, neutrino and proton-decay experiments from 1960 until the mines closed in 1993.
summary.technical: Deep gold-mine levels at Kolar Gold Fields, Karnataka (Champion Reef mine and others): sites of the 1965 atmospheric-neutrino telescopes and of the Phase I (7000 m.w.e.) and Phase II (6045 m.w.e.) proton-decay detectors. Marked with an approximate point at the town.
